name: Outlet polling mixed-load validation

fixtures.credentials: Private inputs only; never include in result bundles

checks: All twenty state-poll slots complete 12–14 successful reads in the observation window.
The longest healthy per-slot state-poll gap is less than 12.5 seconds.
Each of nineteen standalone slots completes two energy refreshes, separated by 57.5–62.5 seconds; no per-socket energy request is introduced.
No more than three background starts occur in any 100 ms window, and peak background concurrency equals three.
Each simulator receives exactly two full-module requests and 12–14 state reads during the steady window, without writes.
A simulated external state change produces the confirmed event within twelve seconds.
With all three background permits occupied, a simulator command confirms within two seconds while a fourth background request remains queued.
Both real outlets remain at their observed initial relay states; no physical switching command is issued.
All temporary entities, simulated endpoints and owned processor fixtures are stopped/removed; the exact processor reservation is released.
report: successful state reads and maximum gap
peak starts per 100 ms and background concurrency
limits: Two physical outlets plus simulations do not establish performance of twenty physical devices.
The simulation protocol is legacy XOR; supported SMART standalone behavior is exercised only by matching available real hardware.
SMART strips retain the existing full child-list refresh; this protocol does not qualify lightweight SMART-strip energy traffic.
Offline, slow or reconnecting endpoints can extend polling gaps beyond the healthy-device budget.
Do not substitute a command acknowledgement for independently confirmed state.
